title: Suspicious Account Verification Alert

scenario.subject: URGENT: Your Account Has Been Locked - Verify Identity Now
scenario.body:
Dear Valued Customer,

We detected suspicious login activity from an unknown IP address (192.168.1.99, Bucharest, RO). For your protection, your account has been temporarily locked.

You MUST verify your full card number and identity within 2 hours or your account will be permanently closed and remaining balance frozen.
scenario.context: Simulated PayPal spoof email with typo-squatted domain and false urgency.

options.text: SAFE — Legitimate notification from payment provider
SUSPICIOUS — Need to verify via official mobile app first
PHISHING — Fake typo domain (paypa1), artificial urgency & credential harvesting

indicators.description: Typo-squatted sender domain ('paypa1' with number 1 instead of 'l')
Artificial 2-hour deadline to induce panic
Requests full credit card number over an unverified link
Destination link points to third-party domain 'paypa1-account-restore.com'

explanation: This email uses classic typo-squatting ('paypa1' instead of 'paypal'), severe artificial urgency (2-hour limit), and aggressive credential harvesting. Legitimate financial institutions never demand card details via urgent email links.
hints: Look closely at the letters in the sender email address domain.
Why is the email forcing an immediate 2-hour deadline?
Does the destination link match the genuine company domain?
learningObjective: Spot typo-squatting, artificial urgency, and fraudulent account lock threats.
consequenceChain: You clicked the fake PayPal restore link
A spoofed login portal loaded asking for card credentials
You submitted card details to attacker's harvesting server
Attacker initiated fraudulent international wire transfer
recoverySteps: Immediately freeze associated debit/credit cards with your bank
Change primary account password from an isolated trusted browser
Enable hardware token or authenticator app 2FA
Report domain to anti-phishing clearinghouse

title: Routine Security Update Notification

scenario.subject: [GitHub] Security update for your account
scenario.body:
Hi there,

We wanted to let you know that a new device signed into your account on GitHub.com.

Device: Chrome on Windows
IP Address: 192.168.1.1

If this was you, you don't need to do anything. If this wasn't you, please review your security settings.
scenario.context: A routine login notification from a legitimate service.

options.text: SAFE - Legitimate login notification
PHISHING - Attempting to steal credentials

indicators.description: Legitimate sender domain (github.com)
No artificial urgency

explanation: This is a legitimate login notification. It comes from the correct domain (github.com), does not contain any suspicious links, and does not ask you for your credentials or create artificial urgency.

title: Corporate IT Mandatory Password Reset

scenario.subject: Action Required: Company-Wide Security Certificate Upgrade
scenario.body:
All Employees:

Our IT systems are undergoing a mandatory SSL/TLS certificate migration. In order to maintain active access to VPN and internal servers, all staff must re-authenticate their single sign-on (SSO) credentials immediately.
scenario.context: Fake IT desk email targeting corporate employees.

options.text: SAFE — Standard IT maintenance email
SUSPICIOUS — Check IT helpdesk ticketing portal first
PHISHING — External domain '.net' and unverified SSO URL

indicators.description: External '.net' domain instead of official internal '.com' corporate intranet
Directs employees to submit enterprise SSO credentials externally
Generic 'All Employees' greeting with no personalized staff ID

explanation: Attackers frequently impersonate internal IT departments using plausible technical jargon (SSL migration, VPN maintenance). Always verify internal IT requests via internal company chat or approved IT service desks.
hints: Check the top-level domain (.net vs your company domain).
Would IT require password entry directly on a newly emailed link?
Verify via your company's established helpdesk channel.
learningObjective: Recognize corporate IT impersonation and credential phishing targeting internal SSO.
consequenceChain: You entered SSO login credentials on the fake portal
Attacker obtained enterprise session token
Attacker bypassed boundary firewall and accessed internal file share
recoverySteps: Notify Security Operations Center (SOC) immediately
Trigger global enterprise session revocation
Reset enterprise Active Directory password

title: Cloud Storage Shared Document Invitation

scenario.subject: Sarah Jenkins shared 'Q4_Executive_Compensation_Confidential.pdf' with you
scenario.body:
Sarah Jenkins (sjenkins@partner-consulting.example) has invited you to view the confidential executive document.

Click below to decrypt and review the PDF securely.
scenario.context: Simulated cloud sharing notification with malicious HTML attachment and curiosity bait.

options.text: SAFE — Regular shared document preview
SUSPICIOUS — Need to ask Sarah directly before opening
PHISHING — Double extension (.pdf.html) and curiosity-lure targeting

indicators.description: Double extension (.pdf.html) concealing malicious HTML script
High-interest bait ('Executive Compensation') triggering curiosity
Untrusted third-party viewer domain 'clouddrive-viewer.online'

explanation: Attackers exploit curiosity through sensational document names (salaries, layoffs). The double extension (.pdf.html) opens a browser page designed to harvest email login details rather than a real PDF.
hints: Look carefully at the full extension of the attached file.
Does the hosting domain match legitimate cloud storage providers?
Why would compensation files be sent unexpectedly from an unfamiliar address?
learningObjective: Detect deceptive file extensions (.pdf.html) and curiosity-driven social engineering.
consequenceChain: You downloaded and executed the HTML file
Local browser ran encoded credential stealer script
Browser stored cookies and saved passwords exfiltrated
recoverySteps: Disconnect machine from local network
Clear all stored browser session tokens and credentials
Run offline malware endpoint scan

title: Package Delivery Reschedule Fee

scenario.subject: Delivery Attempt Failed: Parcel #US-98319-X requires $1.85 customs redelivery fee
scenario.body:
Your package could not be delivered on September 09 due to an incomplete address and an unpaid customs clearance fee ($1.85 USD).

Please settle this minor fee online to reschedule delivery for tomorrow morning.
scenario.context: Small-fee smishing/phishing tricking users into submitting payment card details.

options.text: SAFE — Only $1.85 fee, standard for customs
SUSPICIOUS — Check tracking code directly on the official courier website
PHISHING — Micro-fee scam designed to steal complete credit card data

indicators.description: Trivial fee ($1.85) designed to lower victim skepticism
Unregistered generic .info domain
Demands credit card CVV and billing address under guise of shipping fee

explanation: The 'low delivery fee' is one of the most widespread scams worldwide. Victims readily enter payment details because $1.85 seems harmless, but attackers use the captured card for thousands in unauthorized charges.
hints: Why is the fee intentionally set so low?
Are you actually expecting a package with this tracking ID?
Look at the .info top level domain.
learningObjective: Recognize micro-transaction phishing schemes designed for full credit card theft.
consequenceChain: You entered card number and CVV for the $1.85 charge
Attacker charged multiple large unauthorized online purchases
Banking app alerted to suspicious merchant activity
recoverySteps: Lock the card in banking app immediately
Dispute unauthorized transactions with fraud department
Request new card with refreshed CVV and PAN

title: Vendor Invoice Bank Account Update Notice

scenario.subject: RE: Outstanding Invoice #INV-2024-884 - Updated Wire Transfer Instructions
scenario.body:
Hi Accounting Team,

Please note our primary merchant bank account has changed due to our annual banking audit. Kindly remit payment for the attached invoice ($14,250.00) using our new wire routing coordinates in Denver.

Please confirm receipt of updated banking details.
scenario.context: Business Email Compromise (BEC) invoice fraud targeting corporate accounts payable.

options.text: SAFE — Normal vendor invoice adjustment
SUSPICIOUS — Call known vendor rep on established phone number to verify wire change
PHISHING — BEC attack attempting fraudulent wire redirection

indicators.description: Sudden request to redirect wire transfers to a new bank account
Lookalike domain (.co instead of established .com)
No out-of-band phone confirmation provided for high-value transfer

explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) accounts for billions in corporate losses annually. Legitimate wire transfer detail changes should ALWAYS require secondary verbal verification via a pre-established trusted phone number.
hints: What process should always be followed before altering wire transfer banking coordinates?
Compare the sender domain suffix with official vendor records.
Never use contact numbers printed inside the suspicious email itself.
learningObjective: Prevent Business Email Compromise (BEC) and unauthorized vendor bank account wire redirection.
consequenceChain: Accounting transferred $14,250 to new fraudulent Denver account
Legitimate vendor contacted company inquiring about unpaid balance
Wire funds were immediately laundered through offshore accounts
recoverySteps: Contact sending bank wire fraud desk for SWIFT recall
File IC3 / law enforcement cyber crime incident report
Enforce mandatory dual-authorization policy on wire modifications

title: HR Annual Benefits Open Enrollment Audit

scenario.subject: Action Required: Complete Dependent Healthcare & 401(k) Confirmation
scenario.body:
Dear Employee,

Annual healthcare and 401(k) benefits confirmation closes this Friday at 5:00 PM. Failure to confirm your active beneficiary and tax exemptions will result in default enrollment in high-deductible coverage.

Login below with your corporate credentials to review your 2024 elections.
scenario.context: Targeted HR phishing lure capitalizing on employee fear of losing healthcare coverage.

options.text: SAFE — Standard annual HR benefits email
SUSPICIOUS — Check company intranet portal independently
PHISHING — Threat of healthcare loss to force immediate credential entry

indicators.description: Coercive penalty (losing healthcare coverage) inducing compliance
Generic .org domain not tied to company HR information system
Requests tax identification and payroll credentials via unverified web portal

explanation: HR-themed scams weaponize personal consequences like losing insurance or 401k matches. Always access company benefits by typing the official HR portal URL directly in your browser.
hints: Is the email using fear of loss to bypass your normal caution?
Check if this email originated from internal corporate servers.
How do you normally access your company benefit provider?
learningObjective: Identify coercive HR/payroll credential harvesting lures.
consequenceChain: You submitted employee ID and Social Security number
Attacker diverted payroll direct deposit to prepaid debit account
Identity theft claims filed under employee tax record
recoverySteps: Alert HR and payroll department to freeze direct deposit routing
Place fraud alert on major credit monitoring bureaus
File IRS Form 14039 Identity Theft Affidavit

title: Subtle Quishing (QR Code Embedded in Email)

scenario.subject: Mandatory 2FA Device Migration: Scan to bind Microsoft Authenticator
scenario.body:
Security Policy Update:

Your organization requires hardware-bound Multi-Factor Authentication. Because email link scanners block legacy verification links, please use your smartphone camera to scan the secure QR code below to bind your device.

[Embedded QR Code Image pointing to: https://login-live-auth.online/oauth/authorize?token=9281a]
scenario.context: Quishing attack designed specifically to bypass corporate email security gateways.

options.text: SAFE — Modern 2FA setup typically uses QR codes
SUSPICIOUS — QR codes in emails bypass email gateway URL filters
PHISHING — Quishing attack moving victim from protected PC to vulnerable mobile device

indicators.description: QR code used to evade corporate email URL security scanners
Shifts victim from protected corporate desktop to unmanaged smartphone
Unofficial domain 'login-live-auth.online' mimicking Microsoft

explanation: Quishing (QR Phishing in email) is an emerging technique specifically designed to bypass enterprise email security filters that inspect clickable text links. Scanning the QR code moves the user to their mobile phone where endpoint protections are often weaker.
hints: Why would an email contain a QR code rather than a standard clickable link?
Where does the QR code destination actually resolve?
Has your IT department announced any authenticator migrations in advance?
learningObjective: Understand how QR codes embedded in emails (quishing) evade corporate security filters.
consequenceChain: You scanned QR code with mobile phone and approved MFA push
Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) proxy captured session token
Attacker bypassed MFA and logged into corporate mailbox
recoverySteps: Revoke all active Azure AD / OAuth enterprise session tokens
Re-register MFA device from inside trusted corporate perimeter
Inspect inbox forwarding rules for unauthorized exfiltration rules

title: Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) Session Hijacking

scenario.subject: Completed: NDA_Apex_Holdings_2024.pdf - Review & Download
scenario.body:
All signers have completed 'NDA_Apex_Holdings_2024.pdf'.

Click the link below to view the finalized signed document. You will be prompted for your standard workspace login to decrypt the digital certificate.
scenario.context: Sophisticated AitM proxy mimicking DocuSign to steal real-time MFA session cookies.

options.text: SAFE — Standard DocuSign completion notification
SUSPICIOUS — Log into DocuSign directly to access completed envelopes
PHISHING — AitM reverse-proxy phishing kit stealing live session tokens

indicators.description: Reverse proxy infrastructure relaying real authentication requests to steal session cookies
Deceptive domain 'docusign-envelope-review.net' mimicking official DocuSign
No prior negotiation or request existed for this specific NDA

explanation: Modern AitM (Adversary-in-the-Middle) phishing sites act as a transparent proxy between the victim and the legitimate service. When you enter your password and MFA code, the proxy passes them to the real site and steals the resulting session cookie.
hints: Were you expecting an NDA from this specific entity?
Does DocuSign use .net domains for envelope viewing?
Always access documents directly via your bookmarked DocuSign portal.
learningObjective: Understand Adversary-in-the-Middle (AitM) phishing and session cookie theft mechanisms.
consequenceChain: You logged in and approved MFA token on the proxy page
Proxy server captured valid session cookie 'ESTSAUTH'
Attacker imported session cookie into browser and accessed full cloud tenant
recoverySteps: Invalidate all global refresh tokens and active user sessions
Upgrade to FIDO2 / WebAuthn phishing-resistant hardware keys
Review unified audit logs for unauthorized file downloads

title: Online Market Order Cancellation Receipt

scenario.subject: Order Confirmation: 85-inch OLED Smart TV ($2,499.00 Charged)
scenario.body:
Thank you for your purchase!

Order #MS-992193
Item: 85-inch Quantum OLED TV
Amount Paid: $2,499.00
Shipped to: 742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield

If you did NOT authorize this transaction, call our 24/7 Fraud Support Helpline immediately at +1-800-555-0199 or click below to cancel the order.
scenario.context: Scam receipt baiting victim into calling fake fraud helpline or clicking malicious cancel link.

options.text: SAFE — Need to call that 1-800 number to stop the $2,499 charge
SUSPICIOUS — Check your real shopping account directly from your browser
PHISHING — Fake invoice designed to provoke panic and phone/link engagement

indicators.description: High-value false charge ($2,499) designed to cause panic
Random .xyz top level domain
Prominent phone number routing to boiler-room scam call center

explanation: Fake invoice scams create panic by showing a huge unauthorized charge. They provide fake phone numbers and cancel links so panicked users surrender remote desktop access or financial data.
hints: Check your actual credit card statement or genuine shopping app.
Notice the suspicious .xyz domain in the sender address.
Never call numbers provided in unsolicited receipt emails.
learningObjective: Recognize refund/invoice panic scams and telephone-oriented attack delivery.
consequenceChain: You called the listed phone number in panic
Fake support agent convinced you to install remote support software (AnyDesk)
Attacker transferred funds from online banking while screen was blacked out
recoverySteps: Uninstall all unauthorized remote desktop software immediately
Contact bank fraud division from another device
Format computer if malicious persistence tools were installed

title: Government Tax Refund Disbursement

scenario.sender: National Revenue Service - Tax Rebate Division
scenario.subject: Notification of Unclaimed Tax Rebate: $840.50 Available
scenario.body:
Official Government Notice:

Our fiscal year recalculation indicates an overpayment of $840.50 on your tax records. Because direct deposit details on file were incomplete, you must claim your refund online within 72 hours.

Enter your Social Security Number and bank account details below to initiate direct electronic transfer.
scenario.context: Fake government tax refund email fishing for SSN and full banking credentials.

options.text: SAFE — Government refund notice
SUSPICIOUS — Check official IRS/government portal independently
PHISHING — Government agency impersonation harvesting SSN and banking data

indicators.description: Fake sub-domain '.us.com' masquerading as official '.gov'
Requests full SSN and bank account numbers via email link
Tax agencies communicate refund details via postal mail, never unsolicited emails

explanation: Government revenue agencies never initiate contact via email or text message to request personal or financial information regarding tax refunds. The domain '.us.com' is a commercial domain, not an official .gov domain.
hints: Do tax agencies notify citizens about unexpected refunds via email links?
Inspect the domain ending carefully (.us.com vs .gov).
Never input your Social Security Number into links received via email.
learningObjective: Identify government agency impersonation and recognize deceptive domain tricks (.us.com vs .gov).
consequenceChain: You submitted SSN and bank account number
Attacker opened fraudulent credit lines under your identity
Direct deposit refund was routed to criminal syndicate
recoverySteps: Contact IdentityTheft.gov to start government identity recovery plan
Place permanent security freezes on Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion
Notify IRS Identity Protection Specialized Unit (IPSU)
